source.title: Tensor Normal Training for Deep Learning Models

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The study compares Adam with momentum SGD on held-out classification accuracy and concludes their generalization is roughly similar, qualifying claims that adaptive optimizers perform worse.
record.gate_note: Reports validation accuracy for five optimizers on two CNN benchmarks. Only Adam and SGD with momentum directly map to V4; no random-label fitting, width sweep, convolutional-versus-fully-connected comparison, batch-size sweep, dropout test, sharpness measure, or memorized-example removal is reported.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares Adam and momentum SGD on validation accuracy and qualifies their generalization difference under tuned, decoupled weight decay. It is not an original source for V4.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors: properly chosen learning rate and weight decay yield roughly similar generalization across the tested optimizers, while TNT reaches comparable accuracy in fewer epochs. This is their aggregate interpretation; Table 3 still shows Adam below SGD-m on both benchmarks.
record.recipe_differences: CNN optimizer comparison on CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100; learning rate and weight decay were grid-searched for validation accuracy. Batch size was 128. The paper compares Adam, SGD-m, TNT, KFAC, and Shampoo.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported comparisons vary by CNN and dataset; Adam's accuracy difference from SGD-m is smaller on ResNet32/CIFAR-10 than on VGG16/CIFAR-100.
record.problems: Only two CNN/dataset combinations are reported for generalization. Each setting uses 5 random seeds and shows standard deviation ranges, but numerical uncertainty values are not provided in the text. The validation set is the CIFAR test set; no separate test set is reported.
record.rows_left_out: No other version-mapped outcomes were reported. Other optimizer accuracies in Table 3 were not extracted because the V4 rows compare Adam with momentum SGD, and the remaining optimizers are not adaptive methods named by that version.

untested.parts: Generalization as width increases beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.

Learning-rate-and-schedule-only tuning without tuned decoupled weight decay; language benchmarks; joint broader tuning for classification; switching optimizers; and a controlled comparison establishing whether decoupled weight decay removes an existing disadvantage.
Batch-size effects and adaptations to large-batch training.
Effects of adding or removing dropout.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Removing memorized examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The CNN Adam implementation uses decoupled weight decay, making these results relevant to V4's recipe qualification rather than a clean replication of its limited-tuning comparison. All reported accuracies average five seeds. The CIFAR test sets were used for hyperparameter selection, so these are validation results without an independently reserved final test set.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture and local connectivity.
Language benchmarks, broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, switching from Adam to SGD, and word-level language models.
Large-batch effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout regimes and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to training-test gaps.
Removing memorized examples and measuring resulting test accuracy.
